# Cornelia Bryant

## Overview

- **Age:** Over fifty years old in Volume 1; in her late fifties by Volume 4  <sub>[v1 c9 P44](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0044), [v2 c25 P68](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0068)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v4 c37 P4](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0004)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea, Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>
- **Role:** Housewife and community organizer  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Rachel Lynde's husband (applied to her first husband, Thomas)  <sub>[v1 c1 P2](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0002)</sub>; Miss Cornelia  <sub>[v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>

## Appearance

Cornelia Bryant is a stout, matronly woman with a fresh, pink-and-white complexion and jolly brown eyes. She wears her thin gray hair coifed in a tight knob or cap, and is known for her energetic demeanor. Even in casual or unconventional attire, she maintains an air of dignity and confidence.

_Sources: [v1 c9 P31](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0031), [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c8 P20](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0020)_

## Personality

Cornelia Bryant is an outspoken, sharp-tongued, and fiercely independent woman who prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor. She holds strong, outspoken prejudices, particularly against men and Methodists, often expressing a humorous yet sharp contempt for masculine foibles. Beneath her blunt, critical exterior and caustic wit lies a profoundly kind, charitable, and helpful heart, as she is always among the first to offer practical aid to those in distress.

_Sources: [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v2 c6 P40](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0040), [v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v4 c8 P20](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0020), [v4 c8 P57](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0057)_

- To help those in need and maintain social decorum and morality in her community  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v4 c8 P27](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0027)</sub>

## History

Cornelia Bryant lived for many years as a prominent, outspoken spinster at Four Winds, known throughout the area for her sharp tongue, her vehement distaste for men and Methodists, and her untiring neighborly kindness. She was a close friend and protector of Leslie Moore, whom she supported through her tragic life and marriage. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe moved to the house of dreams at Four Winds Harbor, Cornelia quickly befriended Anne, becoming a frequent visitor and a constant source of local news, sharp humor, and practical help. After maintaining her anti-matrimonial stance for decades, Cornelia surprised her friends by agreeing to marry her longtime suitor, Marshall Elliott, after he finally shaved his beard upon the election of the Liberal government. Following their marriage, Marshall moved into her home, where Cornelia continued her active involvement in church and community affairs, including taking the orphaned Mary Vance into her home to raise.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P37](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0037), [v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v4 c8 P20](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0020), [v4 c11 P29](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0029), [v4 c37 P4](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0004), [v4 c37 P14](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0014), [v4 c37 P28](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0028)_

## Background by volume

- Born Cornelia Bryant, she lived her life in the Four Winds and Avonlea regions of Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>
- Had a brother who died when he was a young man
- Remained a spinster for most of her life before marrying Marshall Elliott  <sub>[v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063), [v4 c37 P4](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0004)</sub>
